title: CompressionBench: How can your coding agents compress LLMs?
abstract: arXiv:2611.06858v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Recursive self-improvement requires AI systems to improve the models and infrastructure used by subsequent systems. LLM compression offers a concrete efficiency objective: retain a pretrained model's behavior within a smaller model storage budget. We study whether coding agents can carry out this step autonomously. We formulate compression as a terminal task in which an agent receives a source checkpoint, storage limit, inference environment, and time budget, then constructs compressed weights and executable inference code. The agent controls its algorithm and experiments; perplexity feedback guides search, and independent verification checks the final model. Across six agents and six model--size settings, 29 of 36 submissions pass verification. translated_title: CompressionBench：你的编程智能体如何压缩大语言模型？
translated_abstract: 递归自我改进要求AI系统能够改进后续系统所使用的模型和基础设施。大语言模型（LLM）压缩提供了一个具体的效率目标：在更小的模型存储预算内保留预训练模型的行为。我们研究编程智能体能否自主地完成这一步骤。我们将压缩形式化为一项终端任务：智能体接收源模型检查点、存储限制、推理环境和时间预算，然后构建压缩后的权重和可执行的推理代码。智能体自主控制其算法和实验；困惑度反馈用于指导搜索，独立验证则检查最终模型。在六个智能体和六种模型规模的设置中，36个提交中有29个通过验证。每个任务选择困惑度最低的智能体设计，相比BF16平均增加3.4%的困惑度，下游准确率为77.33%，而BF16为79.56%。
tldr: 该论文提出CompressionBench基准，将大语言模型压缩形式化为一项终端任务，系统评估了编程智能体自主压缩LLM的能力，发现大多数智能体提交能通过独立验证，且压缩后模型性能接近原始BF16模型。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces CompressionBench, a benchmark that formalizes LLM compression as a terminal task to evaluate whether coding agents can autonomously compress large language models, showing that most agent submissions pass independent verification and achieve performance close to the original BF16 models.
